title: Returning from the second buffer
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over Booleans, let $x,a,b$ be Boolean words, and let $p$ be a valid input-head position on $x$. For every natural number $j$ with $j\le |b|$, running the constructed machine in its backward-through-the-second-buffer state for $j+1$ steps, with buffers $a$ and $b$, their head positions $|a|-1$ and $j-1$, and empty output, yields the configuration in the backward-through-the-first-buffer state with the same input position and buffers, head positions $|a|-1$ and $0$, and empty output.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over Booleans
$p$ is a valid input-head position on $x$
